subject: Catalyst Maintainers pool — allocation & outreach plan
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@hackweek.org>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Catalyst Maintainers pool — allocation request

Hi Soojin and Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. The HackWeek team is finalizing the organizer outreach this Friday and we wanted to lock in the Redwood "Catalyst Maintainers" pool so we can share exact numbers in the public schedule.

Quick ask: can you confirm how many mentor stipend slots and trial credit bundles we can make available to maintainers across three tiers (project leads, active contributors, new maintainers)? We're trying to map expectations so we can publish a signup form and routing rules.

We have a preliminary maintainer CSV (attached) with ~120 projects. If Redwood can indicate tier thresholds (e.g., >100 stars = lead tier) and max per-project credits we will auto-fill the sign-up.

Also: do you have a short blurb (50–80 words) we can use on the HackWeek page calling out Redwood's support and how recipients claim the credits? Ideally same-day claim via a link.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if helpful.

Best,
Elena
---
Elena Martinez
Community Programs, HackWeek Collective
Attachments: maintainer_list.csv (CSV, 2.1 KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@hackweek.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Catalyst Maintainers pool — allocation request

Thanks, Elena — great to see the list.

Proposal (quick summary):
- Lead tier: 20 projects — 3 months of Dedicated-sized trial credits each (reserved quota + 10K inference tokens equivalent).
- Active contributors: 50 projects — 1 month of hosted trial credits (higher token cap but no dedicated capacity).
- New maintainers / community projects: 50 projects — one-off promo bundle for onboarding (5000 tokens + onboarding session invite).

Total footprint: roughly equivalent to a single-month Dedicated pilot for capacity planning. We can mix Hosted + Promo bundles to keep ops light.

As for claiming flow: we can publish a single-claim link that maps repo -> email -> automatic token provisioning (redeem link valid for 14 days). I can draft the 60-word blurb and a short set of T&Cs.

I've attached a quick allocation_matrix.xlsx that maps the tiers to capacity and cost estimates. Two quick clarifying Qs:
1) Do you want maintainer verification automated (based on repo stars/commits) or manual review?
2) Is there a hard deadline for when recipients must redeem credits? We recommend 30 days for onboarding pacing.

If that all looks good Marissa, can you OK the tiers and we will prep the promo blurb and the claim link?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Developer Relations — Community Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachments: allocation_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 9.4 KB)

Soojin — nice breakdown. A few tweaks from budget/dev comms perspective:

- Lead tier: reduce to 15 projects for the Dedicated-sized trial (keeps SLA window manageable).
- Active contributors: keep 50 projects but change to 6-week hosted credits (gives them time to run a mini-demo).
- New maintainers: 55 projects (we can bump one-off promos; community asked to include newcomer workshops).

I attached a short promo-blurb.md you can use on the HackWeek page; it references the redeem link and the claim window (we should be explicit: claim within 21 days).

On verification: Manual review for leads (3-person triage) + automated thresholds for the other tiers. That balances speed and risk.

Action items:
- Soojin: can you publish the claim link + the 60-word blurb by EOD Thursday?
- Marcus: can you confirm there's budget headroom for the extra newcomer bump?
- Jordan: can your team stand up the short-form onboarding email template?

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa Cole
Head of Developer Programs
Redwood Inference
